description: Validator rows (W11Kit-Validation.json) that FAIL or WARN in the VM test for a reason intrinsic to the VM, not to the image. The VM test (scripts/Test-IsoInHyperV.ps1) treats a FAIL/WARN row as expected when the row has hardware=true (the profile's device checks, Wake-on-LAN and the disk health row: the VM has none of that hardware) or when it matches an entry of 'common' or 'hyperv'. Any other FAIL/WARN fails the test. 'match' is a case-sensitive regex on 'Area | Check'; the optional 'detail' is a regex the row's detail must match too, so a real fault in the same row still fails.

common.why: The VM copy of the answer file carries the generic Windows 11 Pro installation key (a VM has no firmware key or digital licence): it selects the edition during Setup, does not activate and is not a licence.

The image enables the Virtual Machine Platform; the test VM has no nested virtualization (Hyper-V: ExposeVirtualizationExtensions off), so Windows' hypervisor doesn't start and the Hyper-V Virtual Machine Bus Provider can't start (code 37). Only that device is expected; any other failed device fails the test.

BitLocker is a deliberate manual step (Enable-BitLocker.cmd, after the key backup locations are chosen); the VM test never runs it, so C: is unencrypted and the row WARNs (DISA STIG V-253259). A protected-but-not-TPM-only drive still fails the test.

common.match: ^Security \| Windows RE on its own recovery partition$
common.detail: ^Windows RE is on the Windows partition \(
common.why: Only if the VM test's disk layout ends up without a usable recovery partition: Windows RE then stays in C:\Recovery. A real install lets Setup create its default layout, which has one. Any other state of the row still fails the test.
The VM has no IOMMU of its own (no Kernel DMA Protection): Hyper-V does not pass DMA remapping to a guest.

hyperv.why: VBS needs virtualization extensions inside the guest; Hyper-V exposes them only with nested virtualization (Set-VMProcessor -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions), off by default and not set by the test.
HVCI runs on VBS (see VBS running).
Kernel-mode hardware-enforced stack protection runs on VBS and needs the CPU's shadow-stack support passed to the guest.

hyperv.detail: S4 offered by the firmware: False
hyperv.why: Hyper-V doesn't offer hibernation (S4) to its guests ('The system firmware does not support hibernation'), so a hibernate profile's powercfg /hibernate steps and this row fail there. A real PC that can't hibernate still fails.

postInstallFailures.description: PostInstall failures (postinstall-status.json) that a VM can't avoid, matched (case-sensitive regex) against the failure text. Anything else fails the test.
